items.title: Goal-based agent loops: set the outcome, let the agent prompt itself
items.why: How I AI's walkthrough builds two autonomous loops — a scheduled PR-manager in Claude Code and a Codex automation that proposes new agent skills weekly. The shift: stop prompting steps, define a validated outcome and let the agent iterate until it's met.

items.title: Launch videos are now a prompt away (HyperFrames, free)
items.why: HeyGen open-sourced HyperFrames: point Claude Code or Codex at the repo and it turns your product's HTML into a polished launch video — Peter Yang's tutorial one-shots it from a live URL. No editor, no budget, no video team.

items.title: Frontier-grade agents just got dramatically cheaper to run
items.why: Claude Sonnet 5 (June 30) runs browsers and terminals autonomously at near-Opus level for a fraction of the price, and OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol preview answers with sub-agent task splitting. Always-on agent workflows that were cost-prohibitive last quarter no longer are.

items.title: Context libraries: many small files beat one big brief
items.why: Teresa Torres's system: dozens of tiny, focused markdown context files with an index, loaded per-task — because too much irrelevant context makes AI worse. End each session with "what did you learn today that we should document?" and the library compounds.

items.title: Claude Code isn't just for engineers
items.why: Non-technical PMs are running research, writing, and personal task systems from the terminal with markdown files — no dashboards, no SaaS. The barrier is one install, and the leverage is agents that work your files directly.

items.title: Evals are the new analytics — an AI-PM core skill
items.why: Aakash Gupta's line: you can't PM an AI product without evals, the same way you can't PM without analytics. If your product grows an AI feature this year, writing evals lands on you — few PMs are ready.

items.title: Adversarial agent debates to stress-test a feature set
items.why: Instead of asking AI for one biased opinion: spin up a 'pro' and an 'against' agent and let them debate your idea for rounds — the surviving arguments define the minimum feature set. Cheap, fast, surprisingly sharp.

items.title: Tool-hopping pipelines: chain outputs, don't pick a winner
items.why: Top PMs don't choose one AI tool — they pipe Perplexity research into a custom GPT for the PRD, into v0 for the prototype, into video gen for the demo. Each output is the next input. The skill is the pipeline, not the tool.

items.title: Manage PRDs like code: version control + background agents
items.why: LaunchDarkly's product team keeps PRDs in git, reviews them like pull requests, and lets background agents keep docs and tickets in sync. Docs-as-code is crossing from engineering into product.

items.title: Query your product data by talking to it (MCP)
items.why: PMs at top companies now query analytics conversationally through MCP connectors instead of waiting on dashboards or SQL help. If your data lives in a warehouse or Mixpanel-like tool, there's likely an MCP for it already.

items.title: Promote agents like interns, not tools
items.why: The emerging management pattern: give an agent a small task, review its output like an intern's, expand scope only after it earns trust. PMs who treat agents as one-shot tools plateau; those who 'promote' them compound.
